name: STRM Sync
description: Writes .strm files for Dispatcharr's movies and series by hand, after each M3U refresh or on a schedule, so Emby, Jellyfin or Plex can add them as normal libraries. Open the dashboard with the Docs link.
author: emby-xtream

fields.label: 1. Where the files go
fields.description: Open the dashboard with the Docs link above. After installing or updating the plugin, restart Dispatcharr once.

fields.label: STRM folder
fields.help_text: The folder inside the Dispatcharr container: the right-hand side of your volume line in docker-compose.yml (for '- C:/Media/STRM:/strm' that is /strm). Movies go into Movies and series into Shows inside it.

fields.label: Dispatcharr address
fields.help_text: How Emby reaches Dispatcharr. It is written into every file, so use your computer's network address, not localhost.

fields.label: 2. When to sync
fields.description: You can always sync by hand with the buttons below or on the dashboard. The two options here can be combined.

fields.label: After each M3U refresh
fields.help_text: Starts once Dispatcharr has loaded the account's movies and series.

fields.label: Every few hours: hours between syncs
fields.help_text: Only used with 'Every few hours'. Counted from the last sync, including one run by hand.

fields.label: Once a day: time
fields.help_text: Only used with 'Once a day'. 24-hour time, in the time zone set in Dispatcharr's settings.

fields.label: Tidy up titles
fields.help_text: Removes provider tags such as |UK|, 'EN - ' or '4K-NF - ' from the start of titles, so Emby recognises them.

fields.label: Also remove these words from titles
fields.help_text: One per line, for example MULTI or [VOSTFR]. Not applied to version names.

fields.label: Add the year to titles
fields.help_text: Only where the title has none. Helps Emby tell remakes apart.

fields.label: Add the TMDB id to folder names
fields.help_text: [tmdbid=...] lets Emby and Jellyfin match each title straight away.

fields.label: Put episode titles in file names
fields.help_text: Off: Show - S01E01.strm. Emby takes episode titles from its own metadata, and providers sometimes send them in another language.

options.label: All movies in one Movies folder
All series in one Shows folder

fields.label: Write .nfo files
fields.help_text: A small file with the TMDB id next to each title. Usually not needed when the id is in the folder name.

fields.label: 4. Versions
fields.description: When the provider lists a title more than once (in several folders, or on several accounts), each copy becomes a version you can pick in Emby.

fields.label: Make a version of each copy
fields.help_text: Off: only the best copy, one file per title.

fields.label: Name versions after
fields.help_text: What Emby shows in its version list. Titles are tidied, version names are not, so tags like 4K stay.

fields.label: Leave out these provider folders
fields.help_text: One folder name per line; * matches anything, e.g. *GREECE* or *XXX*. Folders switched off in Dispatcharr are always left out.

fields.label: 5. How Emby plays the files
fields.description: Every file holds a link to Dispatcharr, which streams from your IPTV provider.

fields.label: Link type

options.label: Xtream link with a Dispatcharr login

fields.help_text: The Xtream link shows in Dispatcharr which user is watching, but writes the login into every file.

fields.label: Only for 'Xtream link with a Dispatcharr login'
fields.description: Leave these empty with the recommended Dispatcharr link.

fields.label: That user's XC password
fields.help_text: The XC password from the user's profile in Dispatcharr, not the admin password.

fields.label: 6. Emby or Jellyfin (optional)
fields.description: Fill both in to start a library scan after every sync that changed files. Leave empty to skip.

fields.label: API key
fields.help_text: Emby: Dashboard, then API Keys, then New API Key.

fields.label: Ask the IPTV provider for missing episode lists
fields.help_text: Dispatcharr only has a show's episodes once someone opens it. On: the plugin asks the provider, one request per show, mostly on the first sync. Off: no requests to the provider, but shows nobody opened get no files. Movies never need this.

fields.label: Most episode lists per sync
fields.help_text: 0 = no limit. Set e.g. 200 to spread a large first sync over several syncs.

fields.label: Pause between provider requests (ms)
fields.help_text: A request the provider refuses is tried up to five more times, after 1, 2, 3, 5 and 8 seconds.

fields.label: Remove files of titles that are gone
fields.help_text: Only files this plugin wrote are ever removed; your own files stay. A stopped sync removes nothing.

fields.label: Removal safety limit (%)
fields.help_text: With more than 10 files, a sync never removes more than this share at once, in case the provider suddenly lists far fewer titles. Renamed files are not counted. 0 = no limit.

actions.label: Sync movies and series
actions.description: Runs in the background. Follow it on the dashboard.

actions.label: Stop the running sync
actions.description: Files already written are kept and nothing is removed.

actions.label: Delete all movie files
actions.description: Removes every movie .strm this plugin wrote.

confirm.title: Delete all movie files?
confirm.message: Every movie .strm file this plugin wrote will be removed. Your own files stay.

actions.label: Delete all series files
actions.description: Removes every episode .strm this plugin wrote.

confirm.title: Delete all series files?
confirm.message: Every episode .strm file this plugin wrote will be removed. Your own files stay.
